    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Engadget ↗ Open Full Page

    Why your smart TV keeps losing its Wi-Fi connection

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (743 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Engadget

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • A smart TV can drop Wi-Fi for several reasons, and most of them have little to do with the TV.
    • It's not uncommon for smart TVs to struggle with a Wi-Fi connection, even if it's been relatively smooth sailing for a while.
    • It's a little tougher for 5GHz Wi-Fi, however, which is faster than 2.4GHz but lacks range and struggles with passing through walls.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    A smart TV can drop Wi-Fi for several reasons, and most of them have little to do with the TV.

    It's not uncommon for smart TVs to struggle with a Wi-Fi connection, even if it's been relatively smooth sailing for a while. Things change, furniture gets moved around, routers are upgraded, fresh TVs are purchased and old TVs are moved to another room. Wi-Fi 6E and Wi-Fi 7 tri-band routers bring faster data rates to the table, but Wi-Fi 4 (2.4GHz and 5GHz dual-band support) is still the most prevalent Wi-Fi standard in the US. For the most part, 5GHz and 2.4GHz are enough for the average household, though it's ideal for most smart TVs to use 5GHz for 4K streaming.

    It's a little tougher for 5GHz Wi-Fi, however, which is faster than 2.4GHz but lacks range and struggles with passing through walls. Your router's features could be making things worse. Many routers use "band steering" when broadcasting Wi-Fi, a feature that combines bands under a single network name, switching your devices back and forth automatically. It sounds convenient. You want your device connected to the most stable band, but it can wreak havoc on your TV's Wi-Fi connection. Devices don't always get the right band, degrading your smart TV's connection stability and speed. For those with older smart TVs, the lack of compatibility could be hampering your connection as well. Older models may not support DFS channels and won't find networks using them.

    Isolate the problem and figure out whether it's the TV or the network by connecting a phone or a laptop to the same Wi-Fi network. If it runs fine, the issue is probably with your smart TV. If not, check your router, gateway or your internet service first.

    Next, check if there's a firmware or software waiting for installation in the TV's system settings. If there's an update available but your internet connection isn't working, check the model name on the manufacturer's website to try and flash an update via USB stick instead.

    According to recent reports, restarting could also be an easy fix. Unplug your TV for two minutes and the router for about a minute. Plug the router back in and let it reconnect before messing with the TV. If the problem persists, go into the TV's settings and clear out the saved connections. On your router settings, turn off band steering and give each available band its own name so you can choose which band the TV will use such as 36, 40, 44, or 48 instead of Auto. If the TV keeps dropping on 5GHz, set the band to a fixed channel outside the DFS range.

    Sources indicate that most smart TV's default to a 2.4GHz Wi-Fi signal to avoid losing connection with your router. This band can interfere with special Bluetooth remote features like voice command, so try turning off the Bluetooth-reliant features on your remote. If Bluetooth is critical for accessibility reasons, switch the TV to 5GHz, bring the router closer, or go the direct route with an Ethernet cable.

    Industry observers note that several factors go into this, including signal strength, network congestion, router placement and the TV's capabilities. If the signal is strong, the obvious choice is 5GHz. Switch to 2.4GHz only if the TV is too far from the router to hold a steady connection with 5GHz.

    Recent findings suggest that speed and crowding are typical problems in most homes because everybody has a device or ten that connects to the internet. A 4K stream needs a steady 20 Mbps (Netflix suggests 15 Mbps, but 20+ is preferable). 2.4GHz has a longer range and handles walls better, but it's slower and usually more congested because neighboring routers, microwaves and Bluetooth devices can all interfere with it. Once you've eliminated band steering and renamed your bands, try each one out. Use your TV's network status screen to make a signal strength comparison.

    Consider a wired connection. A close router makes this option more feasible, so you don't have to run an Ethernet cable across ceilings and under baseboards. If there's just too much space and you can't shrink the gap between the router and TV, a mesh network is another viable alternative. Most mesh nodes have Ethernet ports, so you can place one near your TV and run an Ethernet cable from the mesh to the TV. Just make sure your mesh network has a strong connection.

    Jensen Huang is going to therapy for 90 minutes a day, rethinking his management style, and claims that violating Nvidia’s code of conduct isn’t necessarily a fireable offense. That’s just some of what the newly returned Nvidia CEO told staff during his first all-hands meeting on Tuesday.

    Here are some of the most striking things Huang mentioned during the meeting, according to remarks reviewed by WIRED. Nvidia did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

    On self-improvement: “I go to therapy every day for an hour and a half. And it's been helping me a lot.”.

    In a recent development, on accountability: “There are rumors on the internet that apparently I'm a tech bro, and therefore I’m back. Apparently, I'm a tech bro, and because I wear a super nice jacket, that I'm above the law, and I’m above the code of conduct. That is not true. It won't be tolerated. That is not true. It won’t be tolerated, and it wasn't tolerated here.”.

    “If one of you were to violate a code of conduct, what does that mean? If you were ever to violate a code of conduct, it is not appropriate. I just wanted you to know, it is not right, it's not appropriate, it won't be tolerated. But ‘it won't be tolerated’ does not mean, the moment you violate a code of conduct, we walk you out the door. Facts, circumstances, a lot of assessments. And your management team will still make the decision. That is what is in the best interest of the company and its employees, with all the facts and circumstances.”.

    In a recent development, on his management style: “The intensity I bring elevates everybody else. But I can go too far. When I go too far, it hurts people, it belittles them, it disempowers them. And that’s not right. And so I need to go figure out how I'm going to bring the intensity, the crazy intensity, to the field.”.

    Industry observers note that on women at Nvidia: “I believe we need to create and continue to sustain a safe environment for all of our women. And if I did anything that put that in jeopardy, I cannot tell you how sad I am, and I'll do everything I can to fix it. We will not tolerate that.”.

    In a recent development, on succession: “All day long, this company can run autonomously, and you saw it. I promise you, whether I'm here or not, this company is wired up to execute, execute, and execute, and deliver on financial results and financial results.”.

    “I also didn't believe in succession planning. Let that sink in. I don’t believe in succession planning. I think it’s flawed. The idea of succession planning is not flawed. What people think succession planning means is flawed.”.

    According to recent reports, “There’s a reason why we don’t have succession planning, it’s not because we are unaware of the word. I’m the longest-running tech CEO in history.”.

    It has been revealed that on politics: “There [were] also rumors that apparently I'm back because the highest levels of our government wanted me back. That is also completely untrue. Our board of directors performed their duty as they should have.”.

    In a recent development, “It is absolutely true that President Trump really, really loves our organization,” Huang told employees. “He gloats about Nvidia. You know he does. But there’s a question about politics. Are we now political? Are we partisan? I wanna be very clear with you. President Trump is the United States president. He is my president. And I’ll do everything I can to help this president be informed about how he could make decisions that are in the best interest of our country. … We have to do it, and whoever the next president is will be my president, and I will do exactly the same.”.

    According to recent reports, “Don't think for a second that politics ever play a role in this manufacturer, not even a little bit. We are the most apolitical company. I don't love that we talk about politics here. Take it home. I love that we talk about work here.”.

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1428 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ars Technica

    ⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, on Monday morning, Jensen Huang walked into Nvidia’s Santa Clara headquarters to rapturous applause from employees lining the walkways above him.
    • The spectacular reinstatement of the chief executive of Nvidia, less than two weeks after he resigned in a scandal over an affair with a customer and suspected Chinese spy—as well as a second reported affair with a subordinate—caught even the firm’s most senior executives by surprise.
    • The abrupt reversal by Nvidia’s board was spurred by President Donald Trump, who applied pressure to the board over the weekend after watching what was once America’s most valuable firm as well as the wider tech sector haemorrhage value last week.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, on Monday morning, Jensen Huang walked into Nvidia’s Santa Clara headquarters to rapturous applause from employees lining the walkways above him. Huang was visibly moved as one colleague threw themselves into his arms for a hug.

    The spectacular reinstatement of the chief executive of Nvidia, less than two weeks after he resigned in a scandal over an affair with a customer and suspected Chinese spy—as well as a second reported affair with a subordinate—caught even the firm’s most senior executives by surprise.

    The abrupt reversal by Nvidia’s board was spurred by President Donald Trump, who applied pressure to the board over the weekend after watching what was once America’s most valuable firm as well as the wider tech sector haemorrhage value last week.

    It was the culmination of frenetic lobbying by a “war room” of Huang’s Silicon Valley allies, who pulled in Trump and vice-president JD Vance, according to people familiar with the events. They argued the Nvidia founder was personally integral to the health of the US AI industry, and therefore the stock market and entire economy.

    Industry observers note that “Great men make great mistakes. But nobody has ever been like this, not Elon Musk, not anyone. All the success we’re enjoying, all the tech gains, that’s all down to one guy,” stated an ally of Huang.

    But one of the most remarkable comebacks in corporate history, which called to mind Sam Altman’s brief ousting at OpenAI, still leaves the semiconductor giant at the heart of the AI boom in treacherous waters.

    Nvidia and Huang face probes by the FBI and SEC, congressional investigations, and difficult questions over governance and Huang’s personal connections to a suspected Chinese spy allegedly involved in chip smuggling.

    Even after gaining nearly $1 trillion in market value on the news of Huang’s return on Monday, Nvidia is worth about a fifth less than it was a month ago.

    Huang told employees on Monday he had “made some very terrible mistakes, and I’m going to work on coming back.” Nvidia and a spokesperson for Huang declined to comment.

    The talks that culminated in an Nvidia board meeting late on Sunday were so secretive that even interim Chief Executive Officer Colette Kress was kept out of the discussions, the people remarked.

    Trump personally spoke to the board in Huang’s defense, triggering an about-face days after it had categorically ruled out a return. The board noted it was confident Huang posed no national security risk after “input from senior levels of the United States government,” but that its internal investigation would continue.

    The seeds of Huang’s comeback were sown within hours of his resignation on November 12, which came after reports of affairs with a organization executive and a woman named Alice Huang, an executive at a Singapore-based Nvidia client called Megaspeed, now at the center of chip smuggling allegations.

    Allies in Silicon Valley rallied around him. A small group of Huang’s supporters, including Uber founder Travis Kalanick, venture capitalists Gavin Baker, Brad Gerstner, and Marc Andreessen, as well as Goldman Sachs executive John Underwood, leapt to action, according to people familiar with the matter, making the case in public and in private for Huang’s reinstatement.

    It has been revealed that andreessen Horowitz declined to comment. The other members of the group did not respond.

    Within 24 hours of Huang’s resignation, Baker and Gerstner published an open letter to Nvidia’s board urging them to leave “all options on the table, including the potential return of Jensen Huang.”.

    Their effort had Huang’s backing, the FT reported last week. On Tuesday, Huang confirmed he was prepared to step back into the role.

    Industry observers note that while the board’s chair, Harvey Jones, publicly insisted Huang could not return, Kress spent last week looking to steady the ship with a strong quarterly earnings report and promises to expedite pay rises and equity grants as Nvidia shares plummeted. A organization “all-hands” meeting on Wednesday featured a show of unity from its top executive team, to the tune of Tom Petty’s “I Won’t Back Down.”.

    Behind the scenes, Huang’s allies in his “kitchen cabinet” began lobbying the White House and other power brokers in Washington.

    Recent findings suggest that one arranged a phone call between Huang and Vance last week that lasted 45 minutes. During the conversation, Huang defended his positions on US semiconductor export controls and remote access to chips, and his dealings with Megaspeed.

    Vance, a former venture capitalist who was mentored by Peter Thiel and has raised millions of dollars from Silicon Valley, was seemingly persuaded by the entreaties of Huang and his allies, who are probably a crucial source of funding if Vance decides to run for president.

    “Everyone who was crucial in the tech world was beating his door down,” noted the person.

    “He wasn’t doing it to help raise dollars. That never even came up. But he clearly understands that half of US GDP depends on Nvidia right now… the Nasdaq is up 7 percent. If you think that’s happening without Jensen, you’re crazy,” they added.

    ​Over the course of the weekend, Trump and Vance’s engagement focused on convincing the board that Huang’s affair with Alice Huang did not mean he was exposed as a potential national security risk.

    Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent went out on Sunday to soften his earlier stance, having a week before accused the manufacturer of artificially inflating its revenue through illicit China sales and called for a wholesale leadership shake-up.

    Those involved in the campaign viewed Bessent’s reversal as evidence they were making progress. Trump’s intervention with the board proved decisive.

    On Monday, after Huang was returned to his post, Baker posted on X: “This is why America is the greatest country on earth. Every part of Jensen’s story would have only been possible in America.”.

    Inside Nvidia, employees responded to Huang’s return with a mixture of elation and surprise. Even those who had quietly hoped for Huang’s reappointment told the FT they had not expected it to happen so quickly.

    One longtime employee mentioned that staff who had known Jensen for years were shocked at the context of his downfall, in particular the surge in press reports about his well-known brutal management style.

    Sources indicate that “He has always behaved like this. People of a certain generation are thinking: why now?” noted one.

    Despite running Nvidia for 33 years and owning 3.5 percent of the tech giant, Huang does not have the supervoting shares that enable other founder-CEOs, such as Mark Zuckerberg, to overrule their boards.

    “If I’m Jensen Huang, my first question today is, ‘How can I get me some of those super voting shares so I can tell everybody to fuck off next time,’” remarked one person who had worked with Huang in Washington.

    Huang’s return does not signal an end to the tech giant’s troubles. Trump on Monday mentioned the US attorney general’s office had “done a very thorough investigation” into Huang’s conduct and “exonerated” him. But both Democratic and Republican lawmakers on Monday were outraged.

    Huang and Nvidia’s general counsel, Tim Teter, have been summoned to congressional hearings next week.

    No member of the cabinet apart from Vance had publicly endorsed Huang’s return on Monday. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, himself under scrutiny over Nvidia’s ability to sell to Megaspeed on his watch, was not involved in the board discussions, according to one person close to him.

    Internally, Huang’s personal management style, exercising close control over subordinates aided by his daughter and son-in-law, with no formal succession planning, has led to scrutiny about governance.

    One longtime associate of board chair Jones said the decision to reinstate Huang would do little to assuage public concern and market worries around AI.

    Recent findings suggest that “The midterm elections revealed that the wider public is deeply skeptical about all things AI,” the person mentioned. “The Jensen affair masks a growing market consensus that the debt-leveraged speculative data center build-out is quite fragile.”.

    It also does nothing to reduce scrutiny of Nvidia’s board, which is stacked with longtime Huang allies and lacks any major tech or national security figures.

    “While we are happy to have Jensen back, the on-again, off-again response from the board is, frankly, clown-like,” Bernstein analysts wrote on Monday, adding that it “brings up legitimate questions as to their judgment and process, which has to make one wonder how they come to their other crucial decisions.”.

    Sources indicate that others were more blunt. “Corporate governance has gone the way of the dodo,” said one large Nvidia investor.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Industry observers note that anthropic is moving from having Claude write code to helping developers decide when that code is ready to ship.
    • In a recent development, the latter is the more interesting part of this new set of tools, as AI coding tools already offered code review features before now.
    • Sources indicate that the launch arrives at a time when AI coding agents have become increasingly capable of generating substantial amounts of code, leading to bottlenecks in reviewing and approving the code changes before they go live.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that anthropic is moving from having Claude write code to helping developers decide when that code is ready to ship. On Monday, the newly public AI tech giant revealed the launch of Claude Ship, a suite of AI agents for automating code reviews, fixes, and approvals of routine code changes.

    In a recent development, the latter is the more interesting part of this new set of tools, as AI coding tools already offered code review features before now. What’s notable about Claude Ship is not just that it can review proposed code changes and identify and address problems, but that it also includes an agent that can approve code changes automatically based on policies set by a development team.

    Sources indicate that the launch arrives at a time when AI coding agents have become increasingly capable of generating substantial amounts of code, leading to bottlenecks in reviewing and approving the code changes before they go live. With Claude Ship, the idea is to automate even more of the work involved in the development process, essentially by delegating approval authority to an AI agent itself.

    “Most teams want a person to approve every change, and that’s easy to keep up with when people write every line. But a lot of developers build with agents now,” a company blog post explains. “On the Claude Code team, Claude writes most of our code, and we wanted everything after the PR to move that fast too.”.

    Claude Ship is launching in beta, allowing early adopters to use it to review pull requests (PRs), and then decide what’s ready to merge.

    The fresh offering consists of Code Review, which is already generally available, and two new agents now in beta: PR Steward and Claude Approvals. PR Steward focuses on addressing complications such as failing CI checks, merge conflicts, and feedback from Code Review. It also comments after every push on what it changed and how to roll it back, if needed.

    It has been revealed that claude Approvals then applies an approval policy that the team writes as a file in the repository. This approval process can incorporate various signals, including Code Review findings or the manufacturer’s own classifiers, with policies written in natural language.

    Recent findings suggest that because the offering is still in beta, Anthropic suggests running the approval functionality in observe-only mode first. Teams can also choose to start with just one repository and set monthly spending limits to have more control over the process.

    Anthropic says teams will also still remain in control of where Claude Ship runs, which review settings to use (e.g., Quick, Standard, or Deep), and which changes should be escalated to a human for a decision.

    Claude Ship is rolling out to Claude Team and Enterprise plans for repositories on GitHub. Code Review is generally available, while PR Steward and Claude Approvals are in beta.

    #81653. Why the FAA doesn't want you to put AirPods in your luggage

    📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (764 w)

    Why the FAA doesn't want you to put AirPods in your luggage

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (764 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Engadget

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Air travel rules treat one part of your AirPods differently, and knowing where to pack them can save you some trouble on your next trip.
    • We may receive a commission on purchases made from links.
    • Anyone who's flown in the US is well aware of how fickle passenger rules can be.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Air travel rules treat one part of your AirPods differently, and knowing where to pack them can save you some trouble on your next trip.

    We may receive a commission on purchases made from links.

    Anyone who's flown in the US is well aware of how fickle passenger rules can be. It's only in 2025 that passengers got to stop taking off their shoes during security screenings, and other rules seem to be applied inconsistently. Though some electronics are definite red flags for the TSA, it's possible that screeners at one airport could insist you take a gadget out of your bag, while the crew at another fumes at you for holding up the line. Or vice versa.

    In a recent development, believe it or not, AirPods are another potential point of controversy, despite them being virtually omnipresent because of the iPhone and their noise-canceling capabilities. You should actually be fine bringing them with you to watch movies or listen to podcasts. Instead, the issue is whether or not you can stash them in checked luggage.

    According to recent reports, you might think that would be an innocuous move, but the reality is the opposite, at least if you read the letter of the law. There is some justification, too: the lithium-ion battery in your AirPods' charging case could, in a worst-case scenario, catch fire in the cargo hold, where crews can't easily reach it.

    According to recent reports, according to the Transportation Security Administration, which in turn cites Federal Aviation Administration rules, the main matter is your AirPods' charging case. TSA rules bar you from checking lithium-ion batteries for a variety of electronics, including "portable rechargers and power banks," no matter if they're rated at 100Wh or less of capacity. You may also be barred from checking some other devices with built-in batteries, such as cordless curling irons and e-cigarettes. Don't expect to check your AirPods Max 2 just because it doesn't need a case.

    Recent findings suggest that the threat, according to the FAA, is the prospect of thermal runaway. If a lithium-ion battery overheats, takes damage or is simply exposed to water, there's a risk that it'll catch fire mid-flight, and it would be hard to tackle if it's deep within a cargo hold. Worse, lithium fires are notoriously resistant to conventional firefighting methods. Crews may need to douse the battery with water, since a conventional halon extinguisher can put out the flames but can't cool the cells enough to stop the fire from reigniting.

    Is there a high chance of thermal runaway with your AirPods case? Probably not. Apple tends to maintain high manufacturing standards, and AirPods cases are durable, able to survive plenty of jolts and drops. But all it would take is one fluke to result in tragedy, which is presumably why the TSA and FAA have a strict policy regardless of brand. There's at least some chance of smothering or isolating a fire if you've got AirPods in your carry-on.

    In a recent development, while there are too many international regulations to touch on, as far as the US goes, you should initiative on bringing all of your battery devices in carry-on baggage if they're not being worn, from AirPods and power banks to your laptop. That includes anything you're taking as a gift. For personal grooming, you can save yourself a lot of trouble by putting together a completely non-electric travel kit. Hotel rooms do often include their own hair dryers, you know.

    It has been revealed that when you reach security screening, don't split hairs if you want to save time. If it's electronic, take it off your wrist, off your head or out of your pocket, and leave it loose in the provided bin(s). You should always remove laptops, tablets and e-readers from their bags and sleeves, no matter if a previous airport let you get away with keeping them in. The worst that can happen is that you'll need more bins, and that you'll take a few moments longer putting things back when screening is done.

    If there's any doubt about whether a device or accessory is flight-legal, it's best to either check the TSA's website or leave it at home. In fact, you can save yourself even more trouble by reducing the number of gadgets with you to the bare minimum. You'll probably want your AirPods, but if you're already taking your phone and laptop with you, you can leave your iPad and Steam Deck behind, which will speed up screening and make packing and charging less complicated.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The late Pope Francis suffered a spiritual crisis during his papacy when he struggled with how to lead the Catholic Church and believed he saw and heard the devil on several occasions, according to an annotated collection of his private diaries published on Tuesday.
    • Francis was pope for 12 years until his death last April.
    • Cardinal Victor Fernandez, a compatriot and close collaborator of Francis', collated the diary entries and provides accompanying commentary, in the first set of papal diaries to be published posthumously since those of John XXIII, who died in 1963.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The late Pope Francis suffered a spiritual crisis during his papacy when he struggled with how to lead the Catholic Church and believed he saw and heard the devil on several occasions, according to an annotated collection of his private diaries published on Tuesday.

    Francis was pope for 12 years until his death last April.

    Cardinal Victor Fernandez, a compatriot and close collaborator of Francis', collated the diary entries and provides accompanying commentary, in the first set of papal diaries to be published posthumously since those of John XXIII, who died in 1963.

    The diary entries speak of the Argentine-born pontiff not wanting to be someone "who uses others like puppets," according to the accompanying commentary.

    "It was all mixed with governance problems, pressure regarding decisions to make, and aridity and desolation," a December 2022 entry from Francis said.

    Although the book does not make clear exactly who Francis worried he was using like puppets or the nature of the internal pressures, Francis encountered stern resistance from more conservative forces within the Church as he urged the staid institution to modernize.

    Cardinal Fernandez wrote that Francis "ultimately recognized it was the worst trial that had toremented him ... and that he felt that he was in a continual battle not to fall into this demonic seduction.".

    The 160-page selection of excerpts — starting in 1992 when he was still known as Jorge Mario Bergoglio and running until a few months before his death — are arranged by theme and pay closer attention to Francis' internal spiritual experiences than Vatican politics.

    Recent findings suggest that but one of the three occasions listed where the late pope believed he had seen the Devil was during a meeting with Vatican officials in January 2021 early in what he termed a spiritual crisis. In that instance he even believed to have heard the figure speak.

    Industry observers note that "I can't forget the powerful raspiness of his voice," Francis wrote in an entry. "The Lord granted me an opportunity to leave that meeting, and thus he freed me.".

    Other entries detail how Francis believed that God spoke to him in his dreams, and one from 2018 stated: "Last night I saw the entrance to Hell. I peeked in to look a little, and it terrified me.".

    To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

    The papers show Francis to be self-critical at times, chastizing himself for "feelings of disdain, envy, pride" or for ignoring a drunken man who approached him "because I wanted to have a serene walk.".

    At one point in a 2022 entry he refers to himself as the "proud, self-sufficient, cynical, self-deceptive Jorge.".

    They also show how in later years he felt anxious to make the most of his remaining years, and regretful about some of his deicsions earlier in his life.

    It has been revealed that "I want to do good during the little time I have left, desiring to be good," he wrote in 1996 on turning 60. "How much time I've used badly! How much badly done!".

    The accounts also list his regret after a visit to Chile in 2018 when he faced stern criticism for initially dismissing allegations of sexual abuse and cover-up against a bishop there before later apologizing.

    "It was hard for me to admit what happened in Chile; I didn't think it was so serious," a "devastated" pontiff wrote three years later.

    Industry observers note that fernandez also recounts comments from Francis on some senior officials in the Vatican including his successor, US Cardinal Robert Prevost, now Pope Leo XIV. According to Fernandez, Francis called him "a great pastor, a generous missionary, and an irreproachable man.".

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • A Figma engineer is suing the design software tech giant and its co-founder and CEO, Dylan Field, over allegations that she faced sexual harassment and retaliation while managers and HR repeatedly told her to confront the very people she accused of misconduct.
    • Industry observers note that the lawsuit, filed Monday in U.S.
    • Recent findings suggest that “Figma was my dream company for a long time,” Park told TechCrunch in an interview before the lawsuit was filed.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    A Figma engineer is suing the design software tech giant and its co-founder and CEO, Dylan Field, over allegations that she faced sexual harassment and retaliation while managers and HR repeatedly told her to confront the very people she accused of misconduct.

    Industry observers note that the lawsuit, filed Monday in U.S. District Court for the Southern District of Upcoming York, alleges that Figma’s culture of “direct feedback” led managers and HR to make engineer Serry Park address harassment herself rather than investigate her complaints. Park, who joined Figma in 2022, alleges the organization’s response damaged her career, compensation, and mental health. The lawsuit also alleges that Park, who is Asian, faced racial and gender discrimination, including performance criticism based on stereotypes that Asian women are meek, timid, and conflict-averse.

    Recent findings suggest that “Figma was my dream company for a long time,” Park told TechCrunch in an interview before the lawsuit was filed. “It was a place where I felt that I could level up in my career, working on a lot of really cool, interesting things at scale.”.

    Industry observers note that park is seeking damages, a jury trial, and a court order prohibiting Figma from requiring employees who report harassment to confront their alleged harassers. She also wants the organization to adopt and enforce a process for investigating harassment complaints promptly and confidentially.

    When reached for comment, a spokesperson for Figma noted, “Figma does not tolerate discrimination or harassment. Figma also does not tolerate extortion. These claims have no merit, and we will present the facts in court.”.

    It has been revealed that park told TechCrunch she initially had faith in Figma’s complaint process, expecting that if she documented the alleged harassment and reported it to the right people, the tech giant would act. But as an engineer in a male-dominated field, Park told TechCrunch, “I don’t feel that they took me seriously throughout this process.”.

    Park, who is still employed at Figma, joined its San Francisco office in October 2022. Within weeks, her onboarding mentor — a fellow engineer — asked her on a date and continued pursuing her after she declined, Park alleges. She initially feared reporting him, worrying that her manager would “dismiss her reports or view her as the problem,” according to the lawsuit.

    According to recent reports, park says she tried to avoid her onboarding mentor. In early 2023, for example, she delayed choosing a work project until he had picked one. When her manager criticized her for not being a “team player,” Park explained that she was trying to avoid the colleague she accused of harassment, according to the suit.

    Her manager allegedly dismissed her concerns, saying he had “met his wife at work too” and treating the behavior as “harmless flirtation.” When Park asked to be kept off projects with the onboarding mentor, HR allegedly instructed her to confront him directly about his behavior.

    Industry observers note that the lawsuit ties that response to Figma’s culture of direct feedback, which Park alleges Field established and enforced. It says the tech giant’s People organization trains managers to direct employees, including those reporting harassment, to give feedback directly to the person involved.

    Sources indicate that in March 2023, her manager assigned him to a major project she was leading, despite her request to be separated from him. Park told her manager that she would “figure it out,” but alleges that having to work with him affected her performance. Her manager gave her a 2 out of 5 on her performance review, criticizing her for not speaking up enough or engaging with others and for lacking presence. Park was put on a coaching plan, which she completed in late 2023.

    Industry observers note that changing managers didn’t help, according to the lawsuit. Her second manager also refused to separate them, allegedly telling Park that someone at her level should be able to resolve conflicts with teammates and that separating them would be “avoiding the problem.” Like her previous manager, he allegedly pointed out that he had met his partner at work.

    Park alleges the harassment continued throughout 2023.

    In April 2024, she transferred to another team, a move she claims set back her career by resetting her performance and promotion timeline.

    It has been revealed that on her upcoming team, which had more women, Park said she felt better and no longer had to work with her alleged harasser. Her performance reviews improved, but in late 2025, she alleges another incident of sexual harassment, this time by her new manager.

    In a recent development, the incident followed a night out for drinks with her wife and two teammates, including her manager. The next day, during a team lunch, the manager allegedly remarked Park’s sex life had been discussed the previous evening. Park, who said no such conversation had occurred in her or her wife’s presence, felt “horrified and humiliated” by comments she believed fetishized queer relationships.

    A colleague reported the comments to HR as sexual harassment, according to the suit. Weeks later, Park’s manager apologized in a Slack message, saying she didn’t recall what she had said. When Park sought HR’s guidance, she was again told to address the matter directly with her manager.

    During their conversation, the manager allegedly became defensive, and the encounter left Park feeling “crushed, anxious, and vulnerable.” The manager also allegedly remarked she would never make such a comment because she had “a lot of gay friends.”.

    The manager told HR that they had agreed it was a misunderstanding. HR closed its investigation without interviewing witnesses, according to the suit, even though Park disputed her manager’s account.

    “Requiring an employee to confront her harasser as the price of complaining — and then closing her complaint — would dissuade a reasonable employee from complaining at all,” the suit remarked.

    In a recent development, park alleges her manager retaliated by publicly berating her, sometimes so aggressively that colleagues intervened or checked on her afterward, according to the lawsuit. The suit also alleges that other teammates left the team over concerns about the manager’s behavior.

    Park again complained to HR about “escalating retaliation” and expressed concern the manager would “derail her career.” HR allegedly defended the manager’s conduct, saying the manager was “within her reasonable authority” and again instructed Park to address her concerns directly with the manager.

    In early 2026, Park received another low performance review and a reduced bonus. The lawsuit alleges that similarly situated men continued to receive promotions, raises, and bonuses. When Park reported the negative performance review to HR in March, she was allegedly told her sexual harassment complaint against her manager could not be “substantiated.”.

    Industry observers note that park took medical leave in March to receive treatment for PTSD symptoms and generalized anxiety. Cleared to return to work in June, she was prescribed workplace accommodations, including a graduated work schedule and mandatory remote workdays.

    According to recent reports, park told TechCrunch that Figma approved the accommodations but had not implemented them at the time she returned to work. In July, Park and her lawyers notified Figma of their intent to pursue legal action.

    Sources indicate that “It’s really scary for me,” she said about taking legal action. “I don’t know what’s going to happen next with this, I don’t know what the outcome is going to be, but at least it feels like this is my chance to do the right thing.”.

    This piece was updated to clarify when Park said Figma implemented the recommendations from her medical professionals.

    #81649. Homo erectus lived in the rainforest alongside Denisovans

    📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 11m • 📚 Deep Dive (2127 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Ars Technica ↗ Open Full Page

    Homo erectus lived in the rainforest alongside Denisovans

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 11 min read (2127 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ars Technica

    ⏱️ ~11 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, homo erectus was walking around mainland Asia at least 60,000 years more recently than archaeologists thought.
    • Industry observers note that the chemical makeup of the teeth’s enamel suggests that, over the course of their lives, these Homo erectus moved across surprisingly large distances and made their living in dense tropical rainforests—an environment we’d previously assumed that only our species had ever gained a real foothold in.
    • Baxian and Naxian are a pair of limestone caves that lie 15 kilometers apart along a karst valley corridor in southern China.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, homo erectus was walking around mainland Asia at least 60,000 years more recently than archaeologists thought. A handful of teeth from two caves in southern China’s Guangxi Province just filled in a significant gap in the fossil record of a region that’s vital to the story of how our genus, Homo, took over the world.

    Industry observers note that the chemical makeup of the teeth’s enamel suggests that, over the course of their lives, these Homo erectus moved across surprisingly large distances and made their living in dense tropical rainforests—an environment we’d previously assumed that only our species had ever gained a real foothold in. And one of the teeth offers a strong clue that Homo erectus probably shared this vast landscape with the Denisovans.

    Baxian and Naxian are a pair of limestone caves that lie 15 kilometers apart along a karst valley corridor in southern China. University of Copenhagen paleoanthropologist Frido Welker and his colleagues unearthed a total of nine hominin teeth from among the more than 18,000 bones and fragments from non-hominin animals found there. Macquarie University paleoanthropologist Kira Westaway and her colleagues analyzed proteins and chemical isotopes from the enamel of five of these teeth.

    Proteins in teeth are sturdier than DNA, so they’re more likely to survive a few hundred thousand years. But like DNA, proteins contain variations that can help identify the species they came from. Four of the five teeth in the study had distinctly Homo erectus proteins in their enamel; the fifth seems to be some other hominin species, most likely a Denisovan (more on that below).

    In a recent development, the hominin teeth and the thousands of animal bone fragments had accumulated in a cement-like rock called breccia. Based on luminescence dating (a method that measures how long it’s been since mineral grains were last exposed to sunlight) of the cave sediments, along with the ratios of uranium isotopes in the bones themselves, it looks like that breccia formed sometime between 324,000 and 184,000 years ago. That’s a wide range, but it’s enough to show that Homo erectus lived in what’s now southern China at least 60,000 years longer than we’ve previously realized.

    Recent findings suggest that homo erectus emerged in Africa sometime before 2 million years ago, and they had reached East and Southeast Asia—including the islands of Indonesia—by around 1.7 million years ago. The most recent Homo erectus fossils anywhere else in mainland Asia date to somewhere between 420,000 and 400,000 years ago. Fossils from the Indonesian island of Java, however, reveal that Homo erectus held on in the islands up until at least 177,000 to 108,000 years ago. That makes it a little surprising that nobody had found traces of Homo erectus on the mainland during that 200,000- to 300,000-year gap.

    It has been revealed that these nine teeth help fill in some of that gap, showing that Homo erectus was still around on the mainland all that time after all. On its own, that would be nontrivial, but the teeth also shed light on how these long-dead hominins lived, what the world around them looked like, and how this handful of hominins was related to the rest of their species. And it turns out we’ve been drastically underestimating Homo erectus.

    Credit: Kira Westaway, Macquarie University Credit: Kira Westaway, Macquarie University.

    Recent findings suggest that four of the five teeth that Welker and his colleagues sequenced proteins from clearly belonged to Homo erectus. Careful measurements of the other four—things like the shape and dimensions of the crown, the roots, and the place where the outer layer of enamel meets the inner layer of dentine—suggest these also belonged to Homo erectus.

    But the ninth tooth, from Baxian, has proteins that don’t match any known Homo erectus variants, and the shape also looks decidedly un-Homo–erectus-like, “strongly suggesting the presence of a hominin population other than Homo erectus in Baxian Cave,” wrote Welker and his colleagues in their recent paper in the journal Nature.

    Sources indicate that but who were those other hominins? The enigmatic ninth tooth looks like it belonged to a Denisovan (or Homo longi, if you prefer). But Welker and his colleagues can’t be absolutely sure, because its proteins don’t exactly match any known Denisovan sequence, either (and there’s no clearly identified Denisovan lower second molar enamel-dentine junction to compare it to). But we do know that Denisovans lived in the wider region of mainland Asia at the time, based on fossils from other sites, and there’s no evidence of any other species running around at the same time.

    “It therefore seems plausible that the Homo erectus population represented by the fossils from Naxian and Baxian Cave on the mainland existed in relatively close proximity to Denisovan hominins,” wrote Welker and his colleagues.

    It has been revealed that now, to clarify, Naxian and Baxian Caves weren’t (as far as anyone knows) places where hominins actually lived. The bones and teeth there seem to have been carried in by porcupines, with the result that “why do porcupines collect bones?” is now part of your faithful correspondent’s search history [EDITOR’S NOTE: my search history now includes “there are porcupines in China?”]. So the presence of this tooth doesn’t mean that Homo erectus and Denisovans were roommates. But it does mean they were living in the same general area at around the same time; based on the territorial habits of modern porcupines, the teeth probably came from within an area of less than 100 square kilometers. So there’s a nonzero chance that Homo erectus and Denisovans might have interacted in some way, although we have no way to know what that interaction might have looked like.

    Not long after this, our species revealed up in the area, and we know for a fact that our species interacted, ahem, very closely with Denisovans in this part of the world. Exactly when Homo sapiens arrived is still a matter of some debate, but some fossils from southern China that may be Homo sapiens date as far back as 100,000 or 120,000 years ago, before the major out-of-Africa migration. So for a brief period of time, there may have been at least two and maybe three species of hominins living in the rainforests of what’s now southern China.

    While the enamel proteins from four of the Baxian and Naxian teeth are clearly Homo erectus, they have a slightly different version of one particular protein—one amino acid swapped for another in the sequence that makes up the protein ameloblastin. This variant is clearly different from every other Asian Homo erectus fossil with proteins that researchers have sequenced. That means they’re probably part of a different genetic population (a group of hominins that live in the same area and mostly interbred among themselves).

    It has been revealed that there are a handful of other Homo erectus fossils from elsewhere in Asia that share one amino acid substitution with these four, but the Baxian and Naxian ones have another substitution that the other four don’t have, which means that at some point, their population branched off from the others. By plotting that kind of information on what’s called a phylogenetic tree, anthropologists can begin to map out how different groups of Homo erectus are related and how they may have moved around in time and space. And what we’re learning is pretty cool.

    Recent findings suggest that “The phylogenetic analysis suggests that, although based on sparse data, this hominin population [at Baxian and Naxian Caves] might have diverged before the divergence of the common ancestor of modern humans, Neanderthals, and Denisovans,” wrote Welker and his colleagues. That divergence happened more than 600,000 years ago. And half a millennium after that, it seems, one group of Homo erectus still living in southern Asia may have met some long-lost cousins.

    Isotopes of the chemical elements carbon and oxygen in the enamel of not just the Homo erectus teeth, but teeth from several animal species like elephants (both the pygmy Stegodon and the full-size version), rhinos, apes, and relatives of modern cattle, strongly point to the area around Baxian and Naxian Caves having been a densely canopied tropical rainforest during the Middle Pleistocene.

    In a recent development, different types of plants use slightly different chemical processes to do photosynthesis, so they end up with different amounts of the isotopes carbon-12 and carbon-13; the ratios of those isotopes in the teeth of whatever ate the plants (in this case, pygmy elephants and Homo erectus, among others) can reveal the makeup of the local environment. At Baxian and Naxian Caves, those ratios point to a forest where the trees’ upper branches form a thick, closed canopy above the forest floor. Westaway and her colleagues say the signals look very similar to rainforests in the Amazon Basin today.

    According to recent reports, meanwhile, the ratio of two oxygen isotopes, oxygen-18 and oxygen-16, can shed light on ancient climate conditions; higher amounts of oxygen-18, like the ones in all five teeth from Baxian and Naxian Caves, tend to signal warmer, wetter climates. All of those clues together point to tropical rainforest, a challenging environment that most anthropologists had previously assumed that only Homo sapiens were clever and adaptable enough to make a living in.

    That idea, that we were the only hominins capable of making a go of it in tropical rainforests, was so entrenched that it has been considered a possible explanation for the lack of Homo erectus fossils in southern Asia after about 400,000 years ago. Around this time, the climate became warmer and wetter, allowing dense, closed-canopy tropical rainforests to spread.

    “In southeast Asia, recent isotopic observations of […] expansion of rainforest in the Middle to early Late Pleistocene have been associated with the disappearance of non-Homo sapiens hominin taxa, seemingly unable to shift from mixed savanna-woodland habitats to these increasingly closed forests,” wrote Westaway and her colleagues.

    Even on Java, where Homo erectus lasted until almost 100,000 years ago, those last groups seem to have lived in small patches of more open woodlands, while rainforests spread across the rest of the islands—another correlation that gives anthropologists reason to think the spread of rainforests may have had a hand in the extinction of Homo erectus.

    However, the evidence from Baxian and Naxian Caves suggests Homo erectus could survive in the rainforest, “even if such habitats did not represent its primary ecological niche,” as Westaway and her colleagues put it. That doesn’t mean that every group of Homo erectus was as successful at adapting to spreading rainforests—it’s safe to assume there were cultural and social differences among the groups that might have made some more adaptable than others. But it does mean that we’ve been drastically underestimating our late cousins, and we may need to rethink what we’ve assumed were the limits of their world.

    Other evidence in the enamel of the Baxian and Naxian Caves teeth underscores that point, revealing that a few of these Homo erectus individuals spent their childhoods as much as 250 kilometers away from the cave where their teeth ended up. Bedrock in different places has different ratios of the isotopes strontium-87 and strontium-86; plants take up dissolved strontium through their roots, and eventually it replaces some of the calcium in the bones (or tooth enamel) of the animals that eat the plants. So the ratio of strontium isotopes in your bones can be traced to the area of bedrock where your food was grown during the final years of your life, while the ratio in your tooth enamel is a souvenir of the bedrock where your food was grown when you were around 2 to 6 years old and forming your adult teeth. (Modern food systems are going to be a massive headache for future archaeologists.).

    Industry observers note that all four Homo erectus teeth that Westaway and her colleagues studied suggested that their erstwhile owners had either moved around between different areas or ate food gathered from different areas when they were very young. Some of those strontium ratios match bedrock as far away as northern Vietnam, about 250 kilometers away from Baxian and Naxian Caves, mostly through closed-canopy rainforest.

    In other words, a handful of teeth offer enough fragments of a story to show us “that Homo erectus was not ecologically excluded from rainforest environments and that long-distance mobility into those environments may have been a common behavioral pattern rather than exceptional behavior by isolated individuals,” wrote Westaway and her colleagues. “Whether these adaptations were specific to the late-surviving populations in southern China alone remains to be seen, but further stable isotope work on other Middle Pleistocene sites is vital to address this question.”.

    #81645. The reasons why you should never ignore your car's software updates

    📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (723 w)
    📖 Baca
    AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Engadget ↗ Open Full Page

    The reasons why you should never ignore your car's software updates

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (723 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Engadget

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Hitting "remind me later" every time that pop-up appears may be keeping your car less secure.
    • Sources indicate that your car isn't just metal and moving parts anymore.
    • A software revision is a newly introduced version of the code that runs on your car's computers, and it can change a lot more than the look of the touchscreen.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Hitting "remind me later" every time that pop-up appears may be keeping your car less secure.

    Sources indicate that your car isn't just metal and moving parts anymore. Modern cars are more like "smartphones on wheels," with dozens of electronic control units running everything from the infotainment screen to the engine and the driver-assistance systems. All of that runs on software, and software has bugs. On a phone, a bug means an app crashes. On the road, it can mean a backup camera that won't turn on when you shift into reverse, or even a car that brakes when it shouldn't. That's why you should probably stop pressing "Remind me later" every time your car asks to be updated.

    A software revision is a newly introduced version of the code that runs on your car's computers, and it can change a lot more than the look of the touchscreen. Updates might clear up glitches, false warnings, and trouble connecting to your phone. They may patch security holes that could let someone attack a connected car. They can adjust things like engine or battery management, and they can sometimes add features. Some even change how the car drives. After Consumer Reports found braking problems with the original Tesla Model 3 in 2018, for example, Tesla sent out an update that shortened its braking distances.

    Sometimes called over-the-air or "OTA" updates, revised software is also how many recalls get fixed now. When a safety defect is in the software, the automaker still has to problem a recall, but the repair can arrive as an upgrade instead of a trip to the dealer. Ford, GM, Mercedes-Benz, Porsche, and others have done this. Tesla's recall of more than 2 million cars over Autopilot safety controls was fixed that way, with a free update sent wirelessly to owners.

    Sources indicate that skipping an update means you keep the bugs it was meant to fix, and if it carries a recall fix, that fix never gets installed. Experts say the risks that come with not updating are more significant than the potential complications that come with updating. And that putting updates off can mean missing features and more trips to the dealer, which could ultimately make the car less safe.

    Security patches work the same way, and they're often invisible to owners, which makes them easy to ignore. Car hacking has happened before. In 2015, hackers remotely took control of Chrysler vehicles and shut them down, and Chrysler had to recall 1.4 million cars, with the patch delivered on a USB stick. Tesla fixed a separate, similar Model S hack by sending an revision to every owner over the air.

    Your warranty can be at stake too. GM's 2025 and 2026 warranty booklets require owners to install over-the-air updates within 45 days of availability, and say damage that results from not installing them isn't covered. Tesla and Lucid have similar exclusions. Policies differ by brand (Nissan's 2025 booklet goes the other way and notes owners don't pay for parts damaged by an update Nissan delivers), so it's worth checking your own.

    Industry observers note that many updates arrive over the air, through the car's built-in cellular connection or a password-protected Wi-Fi network, and they usually show up as a prompt on the infotainment screen. If you've been tapping "later," look for an update option in the car's settings menu. Some automakers require a telematics subscription for over-the-air access, so owners without one, such as some Hyundai and Kia drivers, may need to visit a dealer, sometimes for a fee. Older cars without wireless connectivity can still be updated at a dealership, where a technician may reprogram a control module with diagnostic equipment.

    Recent findings suggest that read the release notes before you start the patch. Vague wording like "general improvements" is common, so call the manufacturer if you want details. Install when you won't need the car, with nobody inside and a strong signal or Wi-Fi. Some updates take just a few minutes while others can take up to 90, and many lock the car so you can't drive it. Electric cars may need a charged battery, and some gas cars have to stay running. If an update stalls, moving the car to get a better signal can help, and the dealer is the fallback.

    Democrat Victoria Broderick has won Tennessee’s fourth congressional district, unseating eight-term Republican incumbent Scott DesJarlais in one of the biggest House upsets of the cycle. The victory expands Democrats’ historic House majority in the 120th Congress to 259 seats, the party’s largest advantage in three decades, and flips a seat that Donald Trump carried by more than 20 points in 2024.

    Broderick, 34, a former technology and logistics professional who previously ran for Congress in 2024, told the Guardian in an interview before her race was called that she connected with constituents who had not voted in years and met Republicans concerned about affordability who appreciated the “integrity” she brought to the race.

    In a complete U-turn, Nvidia’s board on Monday reinstated Jensen Huang as the CEO and president of the chipmaker, just a fortnight after he resigned.

    During a meeting before his reinstatement, however, Huang admitted to more affairs beyond the two that have been reported in the news, according to The Wall Street Journal.

    Early in November, Huang admitted to an extramarital affair in a letter to employees. At the time, he was ostensibly talking about his relationship with Megaspeed executive and alleged Chinese spy, Alice Huang (not related to Jensen). Later, it was reported that he’d also had a relationship with Nvidia’s VP of health, Kimberly Powell.

    Afterwards, Reuters reported that he also had an affair with another employee.

    It’s not clear which affairs Huang admitted to during this recent conversation with Nvidia’s board of directors.

    It has been revealed that huang’s return was spurred by a personal intervention from the U.S. government, Nvidia’s board mentioned in a statement on Monday, and President Donald Trump apparently called the board to bat for Huang’s reinstatement.

    Industry observers note that the Wall Street Journal reports that over the weekend, U.S. Attorney General Todd Blanche told Trump and Vice President JD Vance that the Justice Department wasn’t investigating Huang and there was no evidence that he was a national security risk, after which both contacted the company’s board.

    Huang received a “hero’s welcome” at Nvidia’s HQ, with several employees applauding his return.

    Pretty cool, huh? That's exactly what happened to 63-year-old Guy A. Fortt.

    Industry observers note that and there's another concern for Fortt, who, according to IGN, previously had roles in both Jessica Jones and The Sopranos. He doesn't have an Xbox or PlayStation 5, so he can't even play the game and try to find his character(s).

    Recent findings suggest that however, Fortt does have a Facebook and Instagram account. And he posted a video on both detailing his GTA 6 dilemma. Now, according to Fortt in a follow-up video, millions of gamers are essentially on an in-game scavenger hunt to find the character or characters that Fortt played.

    It has been revealed that "I was a motion capture actor on GTA 6, but I don't know who the hell I am,” Fortt explained in his viral Instagram video.     There were also jabs at Trump's search for a new White House press secretary following Katie Zacharia's exit, and at US ambassador to Canada Pete Hoekstra, who is unpopular among Canadians.

    "I mentioned 'find somebody who is less likeable than me,' and we got one," the Trump impersonator joked about Hoekstra.

    It has been revealed that carney stood behind him occasionally laughing. The prime minister also delivered his own zingers, saying at one point: "This is a tough room. And I've been in the Oval Office. Alone. With its newly introduced interior decorator.".

    Both Critch and McKinney - the two impersonators - are fixtures of This Hour Has 22 Minutes, a long-standing Canadian sketch comedy show that has recently enjoyed viral internet fame for its timely skits mocking the Trump administration.

    The skits, published directly on Tik Tok and YouTube, have depicted Zacharia's quick ouster, external and poked fun at rapper Nicki Minaj's, external support for Trump.

    They have garnered millions of views, and even captured the attention of major US media., external.

    Critch and McKinney's appearance at Saturday's dinner is part of an evening of traditionally light-hearted humour, where Canadian politicians poke fun at one another at a gala hosted by the Canadian Parliamentary Press Gallery.

    In a separate speech, Canada's governor general, Louise Arbour, joked about Carney's popularity and frequent global travel.

    "Our prime minister is already getting a lot of attention. Actually, I heard a guy the other day compare him to God. Now seriously, do you know the difference between God and Mark Carney? God is everywhere, and Mark Carney is everywhere except in Ottawa where he's supposed to be," Arbour noted.

    #81638. Breaking: 5 different types of gadgets and accessories you'll want in your car

    EV & Auto ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Engadget ↗ Open Full Page

    Breaking: 5 different types of gadgets and accessories you'll want in your car

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1358 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Engadget

    ⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • We may receive a commission on purchases made from links.
    • There are few things more annoying when driving than when you can't find something that you're looking for, whether that's your phone, sunglasses or those mints you sorely need.
    • Car gadgets and accessories have become practical ways to make your daily commute better and overall calmer.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Stay safe, charged up and organized.

    We may receive a commission on purchases made from links.

    There are few things more annoying when driving than when you can't find something that you're looking for, whether that's your phone, sunglasses or those mints you sorely need. The good news is that most of these annoyances are easy to fix and don't require spending an absolute fortune.

    Car gadgets and accessories have become practical ways to make your daily commute better and overall calmer. You can't influence traffic, but you can make life inside your car more convenient. Some will improve safety by letting you keep your eyes on the road, while others will provide comfort, protection against the elements or simply keep your car from turning into an expensive junk drawer.

    We'll take a look at a few categories of car gadgets and accessories that address common challenges drivers have, including phone mounts and dashboard organizers, dash cams and blind spot mirrors, power solutions, climate and visibility enhancements, as well as organization and storage tools.

    Industry observers note that you get in your car, throw your phone somewhere in the center console or on the passenger seat, and the first serious stop of the day will send it flying. Then you find yourself trying to fish it off the floor while driving — and that's seriously dangerous. Since so much of modern driving involves your smartphone, whether we're talking about navigation, calls or music, where the phone sits matters. Therefore, a phone mount that keeps your device in a stable and visible spot will cut down on how often you glance down or fumble to grab it.

    According to recent reports, there are multiple types of phone mounts you can get. Some clip onto the air vent, others use suction mounts attached to your dash or windshield, while others take over an unused cup holder as a base. If your phone comes with wireless charging and MagSafe or a compatible case, magnetic phone mounts with wireless charging are also an option.

    Whether it's because your own phone is constantly running out of power or your kids are burning through their tablets' batteries, wired in-car charging solutions are always good to have on hand too. These days, you can grab chargers that plug into your car's 12-volt cigarette lighter sockets and accommodate multiple cables. If your car already has USB ports, you could also get some longer cables that reach the backseat or shorter ones that you can use for your own phone up front. Charging devices in the car, by the way, has negligible effects on fuel economy.

    It has been revealed that try to get braided cables since those don't tangle as easily and are generally more durable. You might also want to look into a multi-tip charging cable so you can power up multiple devices, like older iPhones with Lightning ports or ancient tablets with micro-USB ports.

    Recent findings suggest that there are more things you can get to keep your dashboard organized. No one likes the sun beaming straight into their eyeballs, so sunglass mounts are a must. Many cars come with a dedicated cubby for glasses, but you can always buy clips that let you hang your shades from your sun visors. Some come with little magnets, and they're easy to operate with a single hand, while others are literal pouches. You could also grab little trays specifically made for your car's dashboard where you can put things like parking passes. Given their location, however, it's best to be careful about what you put in there because anything metallic, like coins or keys, could turn into dangerous projectiles in the event of an accident.

    Other useful in-car storage solutions are car seat gap fillers that go between your seat and the console so nothing slips through that space. You can also install a little trash can that hangs off your console, or that slips into a free cup holder so you have a place for all your food wrappers.

    In the trunk, cargo nets and trunk organizers keep groceries, tools or sports equipment from tipping every time you turn a corner. Aside from making it so you don't jump every time you hear a bump in the trunk, you're also going to have an easier time with groceries if you don't have to hunt for every potato that's rolled out of the bag. Back seat organizers hang over the back of your front seats, offering pockets for snacks, toys and tablets for the kids, while hooks that go under the headrest make it possible to hang your bag or backpack.

    These days, you absolutely need a dash cam that records continuous footage of the road. With how crazy traffic can be, having proof that an incident isn't your fault is always a good idea. The most affordable and basic options offer front-only recording, but if you want to pay a bit more for more coverage, you can grab a front-and-rear setup that adds a second camera pointing out of the rear window. There are also systems that point a camera at passengers too. Keep in mind that rules around dash cam placement and recording can vary by state, so it's worth confirming what's allowed where you live and drive before installing one.

    Another inexpensive purchase you can make to improve your safety on the road, especially if you drive an older model car that doesn't come with blind spot monitoring, is a set of blind spot mirrors. These small, convex mirrors can cost as little as $10, glue to your side mirrors in about a minute, and widen your field of view, making lane changes safer and easier.

    In a recent development, you also want to ensure you have an emergency kit that includes a seatbelt cutter and window breaker (these are often integrated into a single, two-in-one tool) within reach when you're driving, for scenarios in which you need to escape the car at all costs. You should also have a reflective warning triangle and high-visibility vest somewhere in your car, alongside a first aid kit, fire extinguisher, and an LED flashlight.

    Industry observers note that jumper cables should always be stored in your trunk, or you can even get a battery-powered jump starter so you don't need to wait around for another car to help you out. Before buying anything, you have to ensure that the jump starter is rated for your car's engine size and electrical system. You might also want to look for some extra features, as some double as flashlights and USB power banks.

    According to recent reports, you'll also want to get a portable air compressor so you can handle common roadside headaches like a slow tire leak or a tire that's simply underinflated. These run off either your car's 12-volt outlet or an internal battery, and some models can even automatically shut off once whatever it's inflating hits a preset PSI.

    According to recent reports, if your car already has an infotainment touchscreen with Apple CarPlay and Android Auto, great, but if you have an older model car, you can actually add aftermarket CarPlay and Android Auto screens. You plop one on your dashboard, hook it up to some power, connect it to your car's audio system, connect your phone, and use it to view your navigation app, stream music, and so on like you would in a much newer vehicle. Some even feature a built-in dashcam on the back. For the rear passengers, you can add phone and tablet holders to the backs of your front seats, which usually mount to the headrest posts and grab the gadgets in a clamp.

    It has been revealed that cabin air quality is another area that's easy to overlook. Car air purifiers are a bit bigger than a coffee mug, feature HEPA filters and some even let you put in fragrances as an added benefit. Your life behind the wheel will also be a lot more comfortable if you cover your windshield with a sun shade whenever you leave your car parked outside during the summer.

    • Bangladesh's former prime minister Sheikh Hasina has stated she looks to return home on 16 December, more than two years after a popular uprising forced her from power.
    • Hasina, who has lived in exile in Delhi since August 2024, has asked the Bangladeshi government to fly her back to Dhaka, her spokesperson said.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sheikh Hasina has been living in exile in India since 2024.

    Bangladesh's former prime minister Sheikh Hasina has stated she looks to return home on 16 December, more than two years after a popular uprising forced her from power.

    Hasina, who has lived in exile in Delhi since August 2024, has asked the Bangladeshi government to fly her back to Dhaka, her spokesperson said.

    The announcement comes amid renewed unrest in Bangladesh, where supporters of her Awami League party have staged protests despite a ban on its activities.

    Industry observers note that but it's unclear how Hasina will return. Last year, a Bangladeshi court sentenced her to death in absentia for crimes against humanity over a deadly crackdown on student-led protests that ended her 15-year rule. She denies the charges.

    Bangladesh's state minister for foreign affairs Humayun Kabir dismissed the prospect of Hasina returning on her own terms.

    "Sheikh Hasina will not be able to return to the country as an ordinary commercial passenger; she will be brought back in handcuffs," he told a press briefing on Tuesday.

    Kabir also accused Hasina and Delhi of fomenting recent unrest in Bangladesh, alleging that they were backing "terrorist activities" in the country.

    India's foreign ministry did not immediately respond to a ârequest for comment. In April, âthe ministry remarked it was â examining Bangladesh's request to extradite her and that it wanted to "engage constructively with the fresh government and further strengthen bilateral ties".

    Hasina fled to India on 5 August 2024 as tens of thousands of protesters descended on Dhaka, and crowds stormed her official residence.

    What began as student protests against quotas in government jobs turned into a mass uprising against her government following a deadly crackdown on demonstrators. The UN estimates that up to 1,400 people were killed during the unrest.

    On Tuesday, Hasina's spokesperson Syed Mozammel Ali accused Bangladeshi authorities of forcing her into exile in violation of the country's constitution.

    "Since Sheikh Hasina was flown to India on a Bangladesh aircraft on 5 August 2024, she now calls upon the government to arrange for her air transport from Delhi back to Dhaka," he said in a statement.

    Recent findings suggest that the choice of date is significant. Bangladesh celebrates Victory Day on 16 December, marking the end of its 1971 war of independence from Pakistan. Hasina's father, Sheikh Mujibur Rahman, led the country's independence movement.

    According to recent reports, abu Obaidha Arin, an aide to Hasina, described her decision as "deeply symbolic". "We firmly believe that she will celebrate this historic day among her people," he mentioned, expressing confidence that she would once again lead Bangladesh.

    Hasina's announcement - and Dhaka's sharp response to it - come at a time when the ousted leader is seeking to reassert her political relevance from exile.

    The Awami League was banned from political activities in May last year under the interim government led by Nobel Peace Prize laureate Muhammad Yunus, which took charge after Hasina's ouster.

    The party was subsequently barred from contesting February's general election, which brought its long-time rival, the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP), to power, with Tarique Rahman becoming prime minister.

    But the ban has not put an end to street protests by Awami League supporters, who have also called for nationwide shutdowns demanding Hasina's return.

    Hasina, meanwhile, has repeatedly spoken of her desire to return to Bangladesh, even as she has acknowledged the risks of doing so.

    "I know that they may put me in jail or they may kill me, anything may happen, but still I have to go back," she told a gathering of journalists in Delhi over an audio link in August, on the second anniversary of her ouster.

    Hasina's continued political activities from Indian soil have also complicated Delhi's efforts to rebuild ties with Dhaka.

    India enjoyed close relations with Hasina during her 15 years in power and had hoped that the election of a new government in Bangladesh would offer an opportunity to reset ties, which deteriorated sharply after her ouster.

    But nine months after taking office, Rahman is yet to visit India despite an invitation. He has travelled to China, Japan and Malaysia, and skipped the BRICS summit hosted by India in September.

    Discussions over a possible visit in August coincided with anger in Dhaka over Hasina's remarks to journalists in Delhi.

    The two countries have since resumed talks about a visit, but no dates have been revealed.
